description.narrative: The development objective of Second Regional Economic Development Project for Kyrgyz Republic is to improve access to basic municipal services, strengthen competitiveness of selected agriculture value chains, and increase SME activities in the Batken Region. This project has five components. The first component, Supporting municipal infrastructure, basic public services, and capacity building, will follow the GRID principles to identify critical constraints in an evidence-based manner as proposed by the RISE approach. The second component, Strengthening Agriculture Competitiveness, has the following sub-components: Improving basic public agricultural services; and Strengthening Agri-Food Clusters. The third component, Promoting local economic development through the Small Grants Program, will support SME development through a training and small grants program. The fourth component, Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC), is to improve the Kyrgyz Republic's capacity to respond to disasters. Following an eligible crisis or emergency, including climate-related disasters, the recipient may request the Bank to reallocate project funds to support emergency response and reconstruction. The fifth component, Operational Support, will support project implementation, including the project's monitoring and evaluation system, communication strategy, application of environmental and social instruments, training, and financing of incremental operating costs of the PIE.

The objective of the Project is to (i) improve access to basic municipal services; (ii) strengthen competitiveness of selected agriculture value chains; (iii) increase SME activities in the Batken region; and (iv) in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

condition.narrative: Hire, no later than sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, (i) a disbursement specialist, and (ii) a procurement specialist(Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 1, A.4(b)).

Hire, no later than thirty (30) days from the Effective Date, a Project Coordinator to be based in Bishkek with the qualificationsand terms of reference acceptable to the Association (Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 1, 4(a)).

Hire, no later than thirty (30) days from the Effective Date, an environmental and social specialist to be based in Bishkek cityand one environmental specialist and one social specialist to be based in Batken city with the qualifications and terms ofreference acceptable to the Association (Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 1, A .4(a)).

The Recipient shall establish, no later than sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, throughout theProject implementation period, a Steering Committee, with composition and terms of reference further detailed in the POM (FinancingAgreement, Schedule 2, Section 1, A.9).

To facilitate the carrying out of Part 2.2 of the Project, the Recipient shall entrust the MoA to establish, through an MoA decree,no later than sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, aCommittee for Productive Partnerships, chaired by a representative of MoA and comprised of representatives of MoEC, MoF, stateauthorities and local self-governments and members of civil society, as further detailed in the Productive Partnerships Manual(Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section 1, A.10).

To facilitate the carrying out of Part 3 of the Project, the Recipient shall entrust the MoEC to establish, through a MoEC decree,no later than sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, aSmall Grants Program Committee, comprised of representatives of MoF, MoEC, MoA, PIE, state authorities and local self-governments,and civil society organizations, and, as further detailed in the Small Grants Handbook (Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section1, A.12).

title.narrative: Number of operational productive partnership initiatives

comment.narrative: On track to be achieved by the project closure. The Consultant has been conducting an information campaign, social mobilization, and diagnostics to build a value chain and create productive partnerships in the Batken region and their further development. More than 65 events were held at the level of aiyl aimaks, districts, and cities of the Batken region to disseminate information on Component 2 of RED-2 and knowledge in agriculture, which were attended by 2236 people, including 584 women (26%). Through social networks, the reach of stakeholders amounted to more than 100,000 people. The Committee approved applications as part of 5 PPs (poultry farming, milk, rice, fruits, berries) for further preparation of detailed project proposals. 6 meetings of the Productive Partnership (PP) Committee were held;34 business plans (BP) were approved for a total of 509.3 million soms or (USD $5.8 million) The FCF provided 15 BPs to ARIS for 176 million soms (US$2 million);

"Agriculture" or "Agricultural" includes: crops,livestock,capture fisheries, aquaculture, agroforestry, timber, non-timber forest products. Assets include property, biological assets, farm and processing equipment. Biological assets may include animal agriculture breeds (e.g., livestock, fisheries) genetic material of livestock, crops, trees, and shrubs (including fiber and fuel crops).
